pdfs.text_excerpt:
Machine and Control Building
Session 101L
1
Session 101L
Introduction to VMC Building
Vericut enables you to simulate your CNC machining process. To process your NC
Programs in Vericut you need a Vericut Machine Configuration (VMC). A VMC or
sometimes called a Project Template, is a set of Vericut files configured to enable
Vericut to accurately simulate your CNC machine tool.
This session will introduce you to how to configure a VMC. This session starts with a
Vericut project which has the job-related data already setup, but to have Vericut process
the NC Program you will need to add a Machine and a Control. Once done processing the
NC Program you save your Project Template for future jobs.
The Welcome Screen has opened file:
lathe_session_101l_Intro_to_VMC_building.vcproject
Machine and Control Building
Session 101L
2
First let’s review the layout of the default Vericut User Interface:
Machine and Control Building
Session 101L
3
1. Load a control file for the VMC
• In the Project Tree, select
Control
• In the Configure Control > Control File
• Shortcut = Training
• File = mc_lathe_control.ctl
• Open
Note: The Control file includes rules for how machine codes are interpreted,
associated subroutines, and control settings. When combined with a Machine file,
Vericut can simulate how a NC machine will respond to G-Code NC program files.
2. Load a machine file for the VMC
• In the Project Tree, select
Machine
• In the Configure Machine > Machine File
• Shortcut = Training
• File = mc_lathe_machine.mch
• Open
Note: The Machine file includes machine kinematics, models and other machine
properties. When combined with a Control file, Vericut can simulate how a NC
machine will respond to G-Code NC program files.
• Reset Model
Note: The Reset Model icon causes Vericut reload all files and rewinds the NC
program file. A Reset Confirmation will display.
Machine and Control Building
Session 101L
4
Customize the Vericut Project Template
You have loaded the Machine and Control files and now you will configure the Project
file to suit our needs and preferences.
3. Set Miscellaneous project settings
• Select Project Tree > Collision branch
• Check Machine Collision Detection
• Check Visible Stock and All Active Tools’ Holders; Near Miss = .005
Note: The features on the Configure Collision menu enable you to turn on Machine
Collision Detection and to specify the Tool to Stock/Fixture collision conditions that
you want Vericut to check during processing.
• Select Project Tree > Setup branch
• Fast Feed (FPM) = 300
• Fast Feed (FPR) = 20
• Check the Check Spindle Direction
Note: Features on the Motion tab enable you to provide important settings related to
the motion displayed during the simulation, such as how often the display is updated
(to reduce processing time), setting the minimum and maximum range of the
Animation Speed slider, and what checks are made during cutting.
• Select Ribbon Bar > Project tab > Project group >
Settings > Properties
tab
• Check Enable NC Program Review
• Check Replace Material During Review
• Select OK
Note: The Features on the Project Settings tab enable you to set tolerances for the
simulation, set NC Program Review options and other general properties for the
Vericut simulation session.
Machine and Control Building
Session 101L
5
4. Customize the Status window
• Select the Status
icon from the Toolbar
• Set the window to be floating
(if docked)
• Select a Vertical Tile
• Set Group Visibility
and Group Information display

Session 102L
Build the machine kinematics
The Machine file contains the information required by Vericut to simulate G-Code NC
program files. Machine files contain such information as: machine axes, connect order,
kinematics, 3D models, etc.
This session will show you how to describe the machine kinematics of a lathe in order to
have Vericut process the NC Programs. The Control and Job setup are complete, you
need only describe the machine kinematics.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
lathe_session_102l_build_machine_kinematics.vcproject
Machine and Control Building
Session 102L
2
Building the Machine Kinematics
The following steps will define the components from "Base" to "Stock"
The components to be defined on the stock side of the machine are:
Base > C > Spindle > Attach > Fixture > Stock > Design
1. Build the machine kinematics
•
In the Project Tree, select
Show Machine Components
Note: When the Show Machine Components is toggled “on”, Vericut enables you to
view the "tree" of components that make up the machine and see how they are
connected.
•
In the Graphic Area; Right-click > Display Axis > Machine Origin
Note: the Machine Origin (XcYcZc) axes represents the coordinate system in which
an NC machine is defined.
•
In the Graphic Area; Right-click > Display Axis > Component
•
In the Project Tree, select
Base
Machine and Control Building
Session 102L
3
Notice that the Component Axis displayes the location of the Component
Note: the Component axes (XcYcZc) represents the coordinate system of an
individual component. Each component has its own coordinate system. Components
are defined and connected to other components via the features on the Project Tree
• With
Base selected
• Right-click > Append > C Rotary
• With
C selected
• Right-click > Append > Spindle
• In the Project Tree, select
Attach, right mouse click
Cut

4
• In the Project Tree, select
Spindle, right mouse click
Paste
Note: The same thing could be achieved by clicking on the
Attach component,
then dragging and dropping it over the
Spindle component
The following steps define the components from "Base" to "Turret". The components
on the tool side of the machine are: Z > X > Turret
• With
Base selected
• Right-click > Append > Z Linear
Since the Z axis Zero position is 32.25” from the machine origin, a 32.25” offset
needs to be added to the Z axis component.
• In Configure Component: Z
• Translate tab
• Position = 0 0 32.25
• Press Enter on your keyboard
• With
Z selected
• Right-click > Append > X Linear
• In Configure Component: X

5
• Translate tab
• Position = 19.4675 0 0
• Press Enter on your keyboard
• With
X selected

automatically calculate all the positions
• In the Project Tree, select
Turret
• In Configure Component: Turret > Component tab > Turret Aid…
• In the Turret Aid window

Session 104L
Set Machine Collisions and Travel Limits
The Machine file contains the information required by Vericut to simulate G-Code NC
program files. Machine files contain such information as: machine axes, connect order,
kinematics, 3D models, machine collision tables, travel limits, etc.
This session will show you how to set machine collision tables, travel limits and other
miscellaneous machine setting in order to enhance the Vericut simulation and give you
the capability to detect machine collisions and travel limits. You will test this machine
with MDI.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
lathe_session_104l_set_machine_collisions_and_travel_limits.vcproject
Machine and Control Building
Session 104L
2
1. Set Vericut to detect collisions between machine components
• Ribbon Bar > Machine / Control tab > Machine group >
Machine Settings
Note: The Machine Settings window enables you to configure settings for an NC
machine, such as: collision checking, travel limits, axis priority (for rapid motion),
location tables, and when machine motions are simulated.
• Select the Collision Detect tab
Note: The features on the Collision Detect tab control when collisions between
machine components are detected, which components are protected, and
tolerances used or detecting collisions.
• Check Machine Collision Detection
Note: The Project Tree > Collision > Machine Collision Detection overwrites
this setting
• Select Add
• Component 1 = Turret [Sub-Components All]
• Check [Sub-Components]
• Component 2 = Spindle [Sub-Components None]
Machine and Control Building
Session 104L
3
Notice that the models under the selected components display red giving a graphic
representation of components selected.
• Select Add
• Component 1 = Spindle [Sub-Components All]
• Component 2 = Enclosure [Sub-Components None]
• Near Miss = .25
Near Miss, use to specify a value that controls how close the components are
permitted to be before reporting a collision.
• Select Add
• Component 1 = Turret [Sub-Components None]
• Component 2 = C [Sub-Components All]
• Near Miss = .15
• Select OK
Note: Records displayed in pink are created, and modified, using the Machine
Settings Window and saved in the machine file. Records displayed in white are part
of the setup and can be created, or modified, in the Machine Settings window:
Collision Detect tab or in the Collision and Travel Limits window: Collision Detect
tab and are saved with the setup in the project file. These two windows are linked so
that whenever additions, or changes, are made to white records in one window they
are updated in both windows when you select Apply or OK.

verifying that the machine/control combination responds to G-Code data commands
as expected.

collision tables

Session 106
Introduction to the Control
The Control file contains rules that emulate how a real NC control processes NC data.
When combined with a Machine file, Vericut can simulate how a NC machine will
respond to G-Code NC program files. A "starter" set of Control files are included in the
library files installed with Vericut ("library" folder in your Vericut installation) and can
be used as is, or quickly modified to match the exact requirements of your NC machine
control.
This session will show you how to specify how the Control interprets G-Code words and
special characters.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
session_106m_introduction_to_the_control.vcproject
In this session we will configure the Control to support the below NC codes (words).

included with Vericut installation. This control was purposely modified for this

Machine and Control Building
Session 109
1
Session 109
Configure Control Rotary Settings
As no machine can have the label “standard”, the way machine rotary axes are configured
can vary from machine to machine. Most of the time, the machine manual will describe
how the machine behaves. In this session you will see how to configure and test the
rotary axis behavior.
The following settings on the Control Settings window: Rotary tab, control how rotary
commands are interpreted (e.g. ABC). Each axis is individually controlled. Options:
•
EIA (360 Absolute) — Refers to absolute angle positions. Absolute Rotary
Direction controls how rotation values determine the direction of rotation.
• Linear — Refers to angles on a linear axis "wrapped" around the rotary
component. In absolute input dimension mode (e.g. G90), rotary values
specify absolute locations along the linear-rotary axis, while the sign (+ / -)
controls which end of the linear axis is used. In incremental input dimension
mode (e.g. G91), rotary values specify degrees to rotate from the current
position, and the sign controls the direction of rotation: plus = CCW, minus =
CW.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
session_109_configure_control_rotary_settings.vcproject
Machine and Control Building
Session 109
2
1. Test EIA/Absolute Rotary behavior
• Ribbon Bar > Machine / Control tab > Control group >
Control Settings
Note: Features in the Control Settings window provide an easy way to set the
typical operation mode of the NC control. Control settings are primarily used to
establish default conditions for the control. However, these functions also extend
your ability to detail how Vericut interprets specific types of machine codes, such
as: circles, cycles, rotary motions, and more.
• Select the Rotary tab
Notice that the C-axis Rotary Type is set to EIA (360 Absolute)
• Set Absolute Rotary Direction to Shortest Distance – 180 CCW
Note: the setting Absolute Rotary Direction controls how rotation values
determine the direction of rotation for EIA (360 Absolute) rotary type
components. The Shortest Distance – 180 CCW setting uses the rotation value
and its sign to specify the absolute rotary position. For each rotary motion, the
tool rotates the shortest distance about the rotary center point to the rotary
destination, except when the angle is exactly 180 degrees. When the angle is
exactly 180 degrees, the direction will always be set to counterclockwise.
Machine and Control Building
Session 109
3
Note: The above Rotary Type and Absolute Rotary Direction settings can be
configured (or altered) using CGTech macros from the
G-Code Processing
window.
Machine and Control Building
Session 109
4
• Select the
icon from the Quick Access Toolbar
• Quick Access Toolbar > select
MDI
• NC Block Entry = C180, Add to List
Notice that the table rotates CW even though we have set the control to CCW.
This is because of the Moving Tool Philosophy
Note:
Vericut uses a Moving Tool Philosophy to describe motion directions, and reflect
how the machine maintains the tool-to-workpiece relationship. This philosophy is
used regardless of whether the Tool or Stock component is actually moving.
Consider a standard 3-axis vertical milling machine where the Z-axis moves the
tool up/down, and the X or Y-axis moves the workpiece.
Example 1
Z+ command causes the Z-axis to carry the tool in the Z+ direction relative to the
workpiece. Therefore, using the "moving tool philosophy" describes positive
motion direction as "Z+".

Configure Control to Output Messages
By default, when processing G-Code tool paths, Vericut outputs error, warning and
informational messages depending on what is happening during the simulation. These
messages are written to the Vericut Message Area.
In this session, you will see how to customize an NC control file to generate error
messages, monitor a certain machine status and use model visibility to have a visual
reminder. These methods can be used to add more error checks to your simulation.

Machine and Control Building
Session 111L
1
Session 111L
Configure auxiliary components
This session will show you how to configure Vericut to activate moving auxiliary
components via G or M codes until they touch another component. Typical components
that move and stop once in contact with another component are: tail stocks, steady rests,
hydraulic vises and clamps.
For this session you will configure a tail stock with a quill.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
lathe_session_111l_controlling_auxiliary_components.vcproject
Machine and Control Building
Session 111L
2
1. Define linear axes to move the tail stock and quill
• In the Project Tree, select
Base
• In Configure Component: Base > Append Component > W Linear
• Select a Color for this Component
• In the Project Tree, select
W (0,0,0)
• Right mouse click, Rename
• Change name to Tailstock
• Set the position of the component to 0 0 42
• Add model mc_lathe_machine_tailstock.stl, Position = 0 0 0, Angles = 180 0
105
• Add cylinder model, Height = 1, Radius = 4, Position = 0 0 -1, Angles = 0 0 0
Machine and Control Building
Session 111L
3
• In the Project Tree, select
Tailstock (0,0,42)
• In Configure Component: Tailstock > Append Component > V Linear
• Select a Color for this Component
• In the Project Tree, select
V (0,0,0)
• Right mouse click, Rename
• Change name to Quill
• Set the Motion Axis to Z
• Set the position of the component to 0 0 0
• Add cylinder model, Height = 16, Radius = 2, Position = 0 0 -1.25,
Angles = 0 0 0
• Add cone model, Height = 3, Base Radius = 2, Top Radius = .1,
Position = 0 0 -1, Angles = 180 0 0
Machine and Control Building
Session 111L
4
The tail stock will be controlled with the NC code G53 W and the quill will be controlled
with the NC codes M77 and M78.
2. Use MDI to test the configuration
• Quick Access Toolbar > select
MDI
• Select Axis = W
• Jog the axis to get a feel for +W direction and distance from the part
• Do the same for the V (Quill) axis
•
Close the MDI window
Machine and Control Building
Session 111L
5
The words G53, W and M have already been configured in this control, you will need to
define the behavior for M77 and M78 to engage and retract the quill.
3. Modify the Control file
• Ribbon Bar > Machine / Control tab > Control group >
G-Code
Processing
• Expand the M_Misc
• Add the macros to engage and retract the quill as shown below. Select F1 and
read the help on the CGTech macros
Based on the values you entered for the quill models, set the quill extend value. For
example -11
4. Use MDI to test the configuration
• Reset Model
• Single Step
This will create a
Cut Stock model which is required for the Touch logic
• Quick Access Toolbar > select
MDI
Machine and Control Building
Session 111L
6
• NC Block Entry = G53 W-24 [Enter]
• NC Block Entry = M77 [Enter]
• NC Block Entry = M78 [Enter]
• NC Block Entry = G53 W0 [Enter]
•
Close the MDI window

components via G or M codes until they touch another component. Typical components
that move and stop once in contact with another component are: tail stocks, steady rests,
hydraulic vises and clamps.

1
Session 111MT
Configure auxiliary components
This session will show you how to configure Vericut to activate moving auxiliary
components via G or M codes until they touch another component. Typical components
that move and stop once in contact with another component are: tail stocks, steady rests,
hydraulic vises and clamps. For this session you will configure a steady rest.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
millturn_session_111mt_controlling_auxiliary_components.vcproject
Machine and Control Building
Session 111MT
2
1. Define axes to move, open and close the steady rest
• In the Project Tree, select
Base
• In Configure Component: Base > Append Component > Z Linear
• Component tab
• Select a Color for this Component
• Subsystem = SteadyRest
Note: Subsystems are used in machines with multiple motion components that are
commanded to move via the same G-Code word, for example "X". By default, a
machine uses one subsystem for all motion components, assuming they are
commanded to move via unique G-Code words. When multiple motion components
are driven by the same G-Code word, such as can occur on machines with multiple
independently controlled heads, define different subsystems to control which
component moves when the motion command is processed. Then, configure the
control so that other codes in the tool path activate the appropriate subsystem for
movement.
• In the Project Tree, select
Z (0,0,0)
• Right mouse click, Rename
• Change name to SteadyRest
• Set the position of the component to 0 0 4200
• Add 11 models who’s name contains mc_millturn_machine_STEADYREST
1-11 as shown below
• Position = 0 0 -1270, Angles = 180 -90 0 (for all models)
Machine and Control Building
Session 111MT
3
• In the Project Tree, select
SteadyRest (0, 0, 4200)
• In Configure Component: SteadyRest > Append Component > A2 Rotary
• Select a Color for this Component
• Motion Axis = Z
• Subsystem = SteadyRest
Note: Motion Axis specifies the axis of motion for a linear, rotary or turret type
component, relative to the component coordinate system. Use a "moving tool
philosophy" to specify the motion axis and direction, even though the component
may actually move on the machine instead of the tool.
• In the Project Tree, select
A2 (0,0,0)
• Right mouse click, Rename
• Change name to Arm1
• Set the position of the component to -160 135 0
• Add model mc_millturn_machine_STEADYREST12.stl
• Position = 206 -37 -1270, Angles = -150 -90 0
Machine and Control Building
Session 111MT
4
• In the Project Tree, select
SteadyRest (0, 0, 4200)
• In Configure Component: SteadyRest > Append Component > A2 Rotary
• Select a Color for this Component
• Motion Axis = Z
• Check Reverse Direction
Note: Reverse Direction, when toggled "On" (checked), reverses the component
motion direction.
Machine and Control Building
Session 111MT
5
• Subsystem = SteadyRest
• In the Project Tree, select
A2 (0,0,0)
• Right mouse click, Rename
• Change name to Arm2
• Set the position of the component to -160 -135 0

Session 112
Setting up and using basic debugging tools
This session will introduce you to some of the tools that are available in Vericut to help
you troubleshoot (debug) and correct common errors that you might encounter. These
basic tools can give you clues as to what is needed to resolve a problem.
In this session we will discuss how the Variable window, Call Stack Window and Vericut
Logger Window can be used in debugging your simulation.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
session_112_setting_up_and_using_basic_debugging_tools.vcproject
Machine and Control Building
Session 112
2
1. The Vericut Logger window
• Play
The simulation will stop at the first error:
Error: Work Offset table entry not found: Subsystem = 1, Register = 54, SubRegister
= 1
Note: The Vericut Logger displays all errors, warnings, and informational messages
to assist you during a simulation session. Error and warning messages are preceded
with the label Error or Warning and information messages have no preceding label.
From the start we realize that we have a problem with our work offset.
• In the Project Tree, highlight 1:Program Zero
• In Configure Program Zero change:
• Offset Name = Work Offsets
• Register = 54, then press Enter
• Reset
• Play
Notice that the work offset error is resolved, now the simulation stops at the tool
change
• Reset
Machine and Control Building
Session 112
3
2. G-code Log File
• Ribbon Bar > Project tab > Project group >
Settings >
G-Code
Outputs

and its associated value. When debugging a control configuration, this log file is the
first thing you want to set. Setting up a G-code Log file
• G-code Log File = debug.log
• From the Debug section
Note: The features on the Debug section of the G-Code Outputs tab enable you to
select what debug messages to send to output. Debug messages can provide
additional information that may be helpful debugging development of files used to
simulate G-Code NC programs and simulate machine tool motions.
• Debug Macro Arguments = Yes
• Debug Variables = Yes
• OK
Note: we will use this log file very shortly
Machine and Control Building
Session 112

The variable window is used to track all sort of variables, control or local variables,
and user defined variables. The Call Stack Window is used to easily jump from a
subroutine back to main program.
• Reset Model
• Play

The tool change subroutine is trying to do a tool change for a tool ID that is defined
as a variable CURRENT_TOOL, but what is the value of that variable?
• From the NC Program window select
View G-Code Log File
• Close Log file
Machine and Control Building

5
• Ribbon Bar > Project tab > Project group > Variables >
All
Note: the Features on the Variables panel, are used to monitor, initialize, and
maintain G-Code variables. Most Variables windows are “read only” in that they
display information.

program is calling

Session 254FL
1
Session 254FL
Force optimization
Vericut’s Force is a physics-based optimization method which determines the maximum
reliable feed rate for a given cutting condition:
• Force on the cutter
• Max chip thickness
• Max allowable feed rate
• More…
This session will introduce you to optimizing your NC Program using Vericut’s Force. In
this session we will use the data obtained in session 252T to fine tune the Tool’s Force
Data settings and run the simulation to optimize the NC Program.
The Welcome Screen has opened file lathe_session_254fl_optimization.vcproject

Session 254FL
2
The following steps in this training session will:
a) Select the Force Material File Directory and Stock Material file
b) Fine tune the Tool Manager Optimization settings based on what we saw in
session 252L
c) Run Force in Optimize mode to output an optimized NC Program
d) Review Force Charts to compare graphically the original NC Program to the
optimized NC Program
e) Use Optimize Compare feature to compare in editor the original NC Program
to the optimized NC Program

So, at this point we need to ask ourselves, where do we get Tool Force Data to
optimize our NC Programs? Below are some options:
• Force Charts
• Company database
• Machining cloud
• Tool Catalog
If we use the Force Charts only, we may miss an opportunity, perhaps the
programmed feeds and speeds are to low and that may not give us a good picture of
what is possible with these tools.
Note, the Tool Library file which is save with this Project has Optimization values
which are incorrect. The steps in this training session will have some specific values
for you to set. We encourage you to use your own values from what you can find in
one or two of the above sources in order to better understand how the values in the
specific fields affect the optimized NC Program

This session showed how to build new Stock Material Records interactively during the
simulation. To do this, we had to link cutting tools called by the NC Program to new Stock
Material Records using the Optimization Settings window.

1
Session 11L
Create a Tool Library
A Vericut simulation requires that the below Setup data be addressed.
Required: Stock, Tools, NC Program and Work Offset
Optional: Fixture and Design
In this session you will learn how to use the Project Tree to Setup a Vericut simulation
by building cutting tools, you will build different types of turning tool assemblies using
Tool Manager.
The Welcome Screen has opened file lathe_session_11l_create_tool_library.vcproject
Verification
Session 11L
2
1. Select and open a Tools file
• In the Project tree, select on
Tooling
• In the Configure panel select Tool Library File
icon
• Shortcut = Training
• File = lathe_session_11l_create_tool_library.tls
• Open
• In the Project tree, double mouse click on
Tooling to open Tool Manager
Note: The Tool Manager window enables you to create and maintain Tool Library files
containing descriptions of cutting tools and tool assemblies. The Tool Manager main
window is composed of 6 distinct areas (Ribbon bar, Tool List, Tool Display area,
Coordinate Systems List area, Tool Parameters Definition area, and Messages area),
each with different user interaction.
Ribbon Tabs
Tool List
Coordinate
Systems List
Ribbon Bar
Mesagges
Tool Display
Tool Parameter Definition
Verification
Session 11L
3
This Tool Library file contains most of the cutting tool assemblies required for this
simulation, you need only create tool assemblies for tools 1 and 6.
2. Create a custom diamond insert
• Ribbon Bar > Tools tab > Add group >
Turn
Note: Turn adds a turning tool assembly after the highlighted tool in the Tool Table.
The tool assembly will consist of the Tool with a default Holder component and a
default Insert component. The tool ID defaults to 1, the ID typically corresponds to
turret’s station number.
• Play with the pull-down from Sort by Tool ID
icon and the
Expand/Collapse
icon to familiarize yourself them
• From the Tool Table select Insert
• Select Tool Component
• Select General Insert
• Select from pull-down list Custom diamond
• Inscribed Ø = 4; Note: as you enter values the Tool Display area updates
• Thickness = 3
• R - Corner Radius = 4
• A - Lead Angle = 5
• T - Tip Angle = 60
• Driven Point = 1
Verification
Session 11L
4
• Select Grid
to activate the driven point in the graphics window
• In the Graphic Window, hover the mouse over the center of the tool tip then right
mouse click and select Add Driven Point to Grid Point
Note: The Driven Point option is used to specify the driven point for the insert,
typically the tool touch off point.
Verification
Session 11L
5
• Ribbon Bar > View > Orient group > play with
ZX View and
XZ View
Note: Vericut uses a pre-defined "Relief Angle" of 5 degrees for all inserts created with
Tool Manager.
Note: Use the Undo
and Redo
icons to “undo” or “redo” changes made in Tool
Manager. The icon will be grayed out until a change is made in Tool Manager. Once a
change is made, the icon will display as shown here. There is no limit to the number of
“undo” actions that you can “redo”
Verification
Session 11L
6
Now let’s address the holder
• From the Tool List select Holder
Note: To run a Vericut simulation a holder model is not required. If you wish to
have a holder model for the simulation, the most popular options are to:
•
Use (Block) values to represent an overall length, width, and
height of your holder
• Use the (Sweep Profile) option to access Profile Sketcher window and
create a holder by sweeping a defined profile

• From the Tool Table select
1 > Tool Information
• Select the Arrow new to the Gage Point field
• Select on the holder as shown below
Note: The Gage Point is the point on the tool assembly that will connect with the
Turret station mount point. If the Gage Point is set to 0, the tool will appear
inside the machine Turret as it will connect to the tip of the tool.
Verification

8
• Select the Description field
• Enter 60 DEG, 0.06" RAD. ROUGH INSERT
Note: The description helps quickly identify the tool and its features. The description
will also appear in the various reports generated by Vericut.
Verification
Session 11L
9
Note: The Ribbon Bar > Utilities tab > Preferences group >
Preferences
command button opens the Preferences window, enabling you to control how
information in the Tool Manager is displayed.
Note:
Mark as Default is used to specify an existing tool as the
default tool for that tool category. Default tools become the base tool whenever a new
tool is added in the Tool Manager. Each tool category can have only one default tool
at most.
Once Mark as Default is selected, the file ‘default_tools.prefs’ is added to the User
preferences at the ‘%APPDATA%/Roaming/CGTech’ location. The file is updated
whenever a new default is selected.
Marking a tool as a default cannot be undone. That selected tool remains as the
default for that tool category until a new default is selected so care must be taken
when selecting a default.
Imported elements of a tool (such as CAD, SOR, or Sweep) will not be carried over
to the default tool preference file. Cutters and inserts are also not carried over
meaning that cutters and inserts do not become the default tool components for their
category. Holders are carried over unless “Add Holder(s) With New Tool” is
toggled on (checked) in the ‘Preferences’ dialog of Tool Manager.
Verification

3. Save the Tool Library
• Ribbon Bar > Tool tab > File group >
Save As
• Shortcut = Working Directory
• File = lathe_session_11l_create_tool_library.tls
• Save
Note: The Save Encrypted option allows the user to save an encrypted copy of
his Tool Manager file. The encrypted (.xtls) file can be used in Vericut, but
cannot be modified. The Tool List can be expanded to see tool’s hierarchy, but
only the main Tool Information panel can be seen for each tool.
The Save Encrypted is one-way process, meaning there is no “decryption” tool
to extract the unencrypted files that were used to create it. Users that create
encrypted (.xtls) files are expected to retain and maintain the original (.tls) files.
Verification

• Ribbon Bar > Tools tab > Add group >
Turn
• Play with the pull-down from Sort by Tool ID
icon and the
Expand/Collapse
icon to familiarize yourself them
• From the Tool Table select Insert1
• Select Tool Component
• Select Thread Insert
• Select from pull-down list 60 degree, double end, symmetric
• Width = 0.1875
• Length = .75
• Thickness = .1875
• R - Corner Radius = .002
• E - = 0.093125
• Driven Point = 6
• Select Grid
to activate the driven point in the graphics window

• In the Graphic Window, hover the mouse over the Drive Point in the red area,
then right mouse click and select Add Driven Point to Grid Point
Note: The Driven Point option is used to specify the driven point for the insert,
typically the tool touch off point.

• Select Browse
• Shortcut = Training

6 > Tool Information

Note:
Mark as Default is used to specify an existing tool as the
default tool for that tool category. Default tools become the base tool whenever a new
tool is added in the Tool Manager. Each tool category can have only one default tool
at most.

preferences at the ‘%APPDATA%/Roaming/CGTech’ location. The file is updated

Note: The Save Encrypted option allows the user to save an encrypted copy of
his Tool Manager file. The encrypted (.xtls) file can be used in Vericut, but
cannot be modified. The Tool List can be expanded to see tool’s hierarchy, but
only the main Tool Information panel can be seen for each tool.
The Save Encrypted is one-way process, meaning there is no “decryption” tool
to extract the unencrypted files that were used to create it. Users that create
encrypted (.xtls) files are expected to retain and maintain the original (.tls) files.

pdfs.text_excerpt:
Verification
Session 15L
1
Session 15L
Cut Stock Transition between Setups
With multiple Setups, the Cut Stock is automatically moved from one Setup to the next.
In this session you will learn how to configure a multiple Setup simulation by addressing
how the Cut Stock is to reposition between Setups.
The Welcome Screen has opened file
lathe_session_15l_multiple_setups_simulation.vcproject
1. Cut the Part to the end of the first setup
• Play
Verification
Session 15L
2
2. Save In-Process file
• In the Project Tree, select
Saved IP Files
• Right mouse click Save as…
• File Name = first_setup.ip
• Save
Note: The In-Process (IP) file contains all the data necessary to re-establish a Vericut
session, including the current Vericut model (with previous processing), user
interface settings and a copy of the Log file.
3. Import second setup
A new Setup can be added or copied to the current project. We will import a Setup
which is configured from another project.
• In the Project Tree, select
Project:
• In the Configure Project > Import Setup…
• Shortcut = Training
• File = lathe_session_15l_multiple_setups_simulation2.vcproject
• Import
• Close
Verification
Session 15L
3
4. Step to transfer the cut stock into the second setup
• Single Step
In the second setup, the stock must be moved to the fixture with the machined
surface on the fixture surface.
5. Move Cut Stock to second setup position
• In the Project tree, select
Cut Stock
• Reposition the Cut Stock as shown below using the techniques you learned in
training session 9
Verification
Session 15L
4
6. Preserve the Stock Transition
• In the Configure Model > Preserve Stock Transition
• When Prompted: Previously saved IP will not apply to this Stock Transition. Do
you want to continue? Select Yes
Note: The Message Area Created Transition Coordinate System:
Note: The Preserve Stock Transition option will create the coordinate systems
required for transitioning the Cut Stock from one setup position to another. Preserve
Stock Transition is only active when a stock component model is selected. This
transition will be saved with the project file and during simulation the Cut Stock will
be translated to its new position automatically.
Verification
Session 15L
5
7. Cut the part from the beginning to the end
• Reset Model
• Play
• Single Step
• Play
8. Save Project
• Ribbon Bar > File tab > Project File group >
Save As
• Shortcut= Working Directory
• File Name = lathe_session_15l_multiple_setups_simulation.vcproject
• Save
9. Re-start the simulation at the end of the first setup by opening
the In-Process file
• In the Project Tree, double click on the
first_setup.ip
• Play
Notice that the Vericut session has been re-establish to the state it was in when the
IP File was saved. The .ip file was saved prior to importing the second setup, so
after loading the .ip file the second setup is no longer present. For this we would
need to load the lathe_session_15l_multiple_setups_simulation.vcproject.
Conclusion
In this session, you have seen how to configure a project with 2 distinct setups and
preserve the Cut Stock transition between the setups. You also have seen that an In-
Process file can be saved to save and re-start the simulation.

Probe Programming
The "end product" of Vericut's Probe Programming functionality is to generate probe
cycles generate an NC program (.mcd file) using the probe cycles generated. The
intention is to run the probing program with the part still on the CNC machine to verify
what has just been cut correctly to the design print to ensure that the job is proceeding as
intended. If a discrepancy is found, no additional time will be wasted on subsequent
machining. This goal can be reached quickly if the probing is performed on the machine
and by the machine, using one or more probes.
This session shows how to generate a probe NC Program.

Session 3L
Find and Detect Errors
The main reason we use simulation is to detect all the errors in the NC program before it
goes to the machine. Vericut provides many ways to detect errors and precisely find
which line in the NC program caused them. We cannot always rely on a visual red mark
on the part to indicate an error; the red mark might be removed by the subsequent
machining operation. Vericut keeps a history of every event including the errors.
In this session you will learn how to detect the errors in the simulation, and how to find
the blocks in the program responsible for the errors.
The Welcome Screen has opened file lathe_session_day1.vcproject.
Verification

• Select the Feature Search
icon, type syn as shown below
Note: clicking the Feature Search
option expands a search bar that can be
used to find any feature in Vericut. Options related to entered search queries are
displayed and can be clicked so that Vericut navigates directly to those features.
Hovering over the feature gives it location within the ribbon.
• Select
Perform Syntax Check
Note: Many of Vericut’s functions output temporary messages or prompts to
assist you with using the feature. These messages and prompts are displayed in
the space below the Animations Control features as shown in the picture below.
Note: The Perform Syntax Check option causes Vericut to check all NC
program and NC Subroutine files referenced by the “current” setup for syntax
errors. Each syntax error that is found is written to the Message Area and a
summary showing the number of syntax errors found is displayed directly below
the Message Area.

Syntax.

in the NC program window is highlighted.

Note: NC Program Preview detects any errors that do not require processing the
material removal, example “Fast feed rate removed material”. The errors detected
are: tool touching the fixture, tool violating the design model, machine collisions and

• Ribbon Bar > Analysis tab > Analysis group >
AUTO-DIFF
Note: The AUTO-DIFF option opens the AUTO-DIFF window enabling you to
compare the design model against the Vericut simulated cut model (Cut Stock). Using
AUTO-DIFF, clearly identifies discrepancies between the Cut Stock model and the
intended design model.
Note: For more information on the available configuration options and descriptions
see Vericut Help – Analysis Menu - AUTO-DIFF

Session 8
Create Coordinate Systems
A Coordinate System (CSYS) in Vericut represents a point in space and an orientation
represented by the 3 axes. It can be created in relation to any machine component but is
usually defined relative to the Stock component. It can be referenced to represent the
origin of a NC Program, as a reference origin for X-Caliper measurements and also can
be used to create a transition to move models. You will see the multiple applications of
the CSYS in the subsequent training sessions. This session will concentrate on the
creation of the CSYS.

• Snap the CSYS Origin to a 3D object
Note: You can snap the object to another 3D object’s center faces, center edges,
and corners by hovering the mouse over the transform CSYS Origin, then
clicking and dragging. As you drag the transform CSYS above 3D objects, you
will notice it try to snap to them. You can release the mouse button to apply the
snap.
• Play with the Snap CSYS Origin feature by selecting different locations in order
to become more familiar with this feature
Verification
Session 8
12
CSYS Translation along a Single Axis
• Check Enable Translation Increment and set a value, then over your mouse
over 1 of the 3 Transform CSYS arrows. You should see the arrow outline
highlight light-blue, indicating you can click on it. Click and hold the left mouse
button, and drag your mouse to move the object along the axis.
• Play with the CSYS Translation along a Single Axis feature by selecting
different locations in order to become more familiar with this feature
Verification
Session 8
13
CSYS Translation along Two Axes
• To translate along two axes, hover the mouse over one of the small planes that
surround the transform CSYS origin. Once one of them is highlighted, you can
click and drag to move the object along the plane.
This time, you will see two guidelines, and two numbers show up to the top-right
of the csys. One for one axis, and another for the other axis, color coded to the
axes. Translation incrementing also applies here, and you will see cross sections
appear along both axis guidelines.
• Play with the CSYS Translation along Two Axes feature by selecting different
locations in order to become more familiar with this feature
Verification
Session 8
14
CSYS Rotation along Axis
• Check Enable Translation Increment and set a value
• You can rotate along a single axis by hovering the mouse over a ring to highlight
it, then click and drag around the origin to rotate. You will notice a black guide
ring appear around the origin showing the direction of rotation.
A number in black font to the top-right of the CSYS shows the angle in degrees of
how much the object is being rotated.
Once you release the left mouse button, the rotation will be applied. You will
notice that the direction of the axes have changed. This is normal. This is to allow
the user to translate in defined directions. It also represents how the object will
appear if it is a regular CSYS being transformed.
You can also apply rotations in the ‘Rotate’ number box. Just like the ‘Translate’
number box, the order of axes is X Y Z. For example, 0 0 30 would rotate the
object by 30 degrees on the Z axis. This ignores incrementing.
• Play with the CSYS Rotation along Axis feature by selecting different locations
in order to become more familiar with this feature
Verification
